requirements.title: macOS network integration (feth/BPF/DHCP/DNS/MTU)
evidence: docs/G2-VERIFICATION.md (feth100, DHCP lease, DNS/default route, HTTPS without Wi-Fi)
target/g2-prefer/ (route via feth100 and HTTP 200 while Wi-Fi stays on)
crates/tether-core/src/engine.rs (batched host frames, 100 ms notification polling)
real automated run on 2026-11-01: 3x replug, 1.82 MB/s (1 MB) and 7.35 MB/s (5 MB) download, 1.18 MB/s upload, ping avg 44.8 ms; Twitch confirmed smooth by the user

requirements.title: Lifecycle, errors, reset and cleanup
evidence: real disconnect/connect cycle and 15-minute stability run
real user LaunchAgent installed and waiting for RNDIS
real auto-connect on attach, 3x replug with fresh DHCP lease, and launchctl kickstart restart on 2026-11-01
real sleep/wake cycle: system_sleep -> system_wake, reconnects=1, session restored
crates/tether-helper/src/main.rs (stale default route treated as no default; own bridge not used as fallback anchor)
real tethering off/on cycle with the fixed helper on 2026-11-02: reconnect with feth100 as default uplink, ping 2/2, HTTPS 200, no route abort
gaps: two more hardware sleep/wake repetitions were not run; the user accepted G2 with the current data
tethering off/on was run 3x by the user; only one full session rebuild is visible in the monitor log; a post-fix cycle was verified on 2026-11-02
reconnect uses the existing feth MTU; a device with a smaller MTU requires a manual reconnect
hardware device swap is still open
